title: Control Plane Operational Boundaries Heatmap
content:
Purpose and context:

This is a working heatmap-style sketch to surface current operational boundaries in the control plane: who owns what during normal ops and during multi-region failover. Goal is to call out ambiguous gaps and create a short list of follow-ups (owner assignments, runbook updates, API contracts). Not a canonical doc — an annotated work-in-progress for the platform-engineering and serving-runtime teams.

Assumptions and constraints (short):
- Single control-plane control path (API gateway -> orchestrator -> runtime adapters).
- We support 3 regions (us-west, eu-west, ap-southeast) with regional control-plane replicas and a global config plane.
- Traffic routing is policy-driven: latency-first, then cost, then compliance (region-locked).
- Runtime adapters are the thin bridge to GPU pools and on-prem agents.

High-level ownership summary (heatmap commentary):
- API Gateway (ingest): primary owner = platform-api team. Responsibilities: authentication, rate limiting, coarse routing decisions, quota enforcement, request enrichment. SLA: <100ms control-plane p99 for routing decision. Region fallback: platform-api config points to regional orchestrators; in loss-of-region, global gateway switches to nearest fallback pool.
- Orchestration Layer (request-to-runtime mapping, rollouts): primary owner = orchestration-service team. Responsibilities: model versioning, canary rollouts, route affinity, autoscale hints, batching policies. SLA: transactional durability and consistent rollout state across regions.
- Runtime Adapters (serving proxies): primary owner = serving-runtime team. Responsibilities: translate orchestration directives to runtime-specific calls (CUDA-optimized pools, on-prem RPC), manage KV cache metadata, surface local capacity. SLA: <50ms adapter handshake for pooled requests, best-effort KV cache sync.
- Routing Governance / Policy Engine: primary owner = platform-engineering (routing-gov subteam). Responsibilities: policy language, policy validation, policy audit logs, safety gates for fallback.
- SRE/Infra (ops): primary owner = infra-sre. Responsibilities: infra health, cross-region replication, infra failover, monitoring/alerting for control plane.

Operational boundary matrix (text table):
Service | Owner | Primary responsibilities | Decision boundary | Typical ops handoff
API Gateway | platform-api | auth, ingress, coarse routing | chooses region/orch config based on policy | handoff to orchestration via RPC (orchestration endpoint v2)
Orchestrator | orchestration-service | model routing, version pins, rollout rules | final route decision (which adapter pool) | handoff to runtime adapter with rollout metadata and batching hints
Runtime Adapter | serving-runtime | queueing, batching, KV cache, runtime calls | enforces local capacity and throttles | returns run metrics and fallback signals
Policy Engine | routing-gov | policy eval, validation, audit | rejects unsafe routing changes | notifies orchestration and platform-api on violations
SRE/Infra | infra-sre | infra failover, region replication | triggers region-level failover | notifies all owners, runs global incident runbook

Key decision boundaries to clarify (open questions):
1) Where is the canonical source-of-truth for route-to-adapter mappings?
   - current state: orchestrator maintains mapping but policy engine can inject overrides. Leads to potential race condition during rollout.
   - proposed: orchestrator remains source-of-truth; policy engine issues signed overrides that orchestrator applies with a reconciliation window (TBD).

2) How do we represent multi-region fallbacks in the API contract?
   - suggestion: add an explicit "fallback_chain" field in orchestration responses listing region adapters ordered by policy priority. This makes failover deterministic for adapters.

3) KV cache consistency vs latency: who owns reconciliation?
   - tradeoff: serving-runtime prefers local fast cache with eventual consistency. Orchestrator needs strong-ish invariants for prefix cache invalidation during model switch.
   - interim: add a lightweight invalidation message bus (owner: serving-runtime + infra-sre) with documented TTL semantics.

4) Rollouts across regions: canaries vs global sync?
   - current experiments: region-scoped canaries for low blast radius. Global rollouts often lag and produce inconsistency in inference quality metrics.
   - proposal: add rollout epoch metadata and a global acceptance gate managed by orchestration + product-eval.

Runbook and incident boundaries (short bullets):
- API ingress failures: platform-api owns mitigation (rate-limits, revert gateway config). Escalate to infra-sre on region degradation.
- Orchestrator inconsistencies (mismatched route assignments): orchestration-service owns reconciliation; if >5% mismatches cross-region, open sev3 and rollback last policy change.
- Adapter capacity exhaustion: serving-runtime implements emergency fallback to pre-defined model shards in another region; infra-sre handles cross-region route reweighting.
- Policy violation alerts: routing-gov triages; if unsafe changes detected auto-revert and notify on-call for platform-engineering.

Small proposal list (next steps):
- Draft an API change for orchestration response to include "fallback_chain" + rollout_epoch (owner: orchestration-service). Link: PLAT-4321.
- Prototype signed override flow from policy engine to orchestrator (owner: routing-gov + platform-api). Add TTL and audit log entry.
- Create simple invalidation bus for KV cache with at-most-once invalidation messages (owner: serving-runtime + infra-sre).
- Update incident runbooks to define clear threshold for cross-region inconsistency (owner: infra-sre).

Notes / references / bookmarks:
- Related PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/control-plane/pull/198 (orchestration epoch prototype)
- Jira: PLAT-4321 (fallback_chain RFC), PLAT-4502 (KV invalidation proposal)
- Slack thread: #platform-routing – thread id: t0239-heatmap-draft

Open questions for the group meeting (TODOs):
- Acceptable reconciliation window between policy override issuance and orchestrator apply? (Suggested: 60s)
- How do we test cross-region rollout acceptance in CI without incurring expensive GPU runs? (Idea: synthetic traffic + small local model)
- Define exact schema for fallback_chain and rollout_epoch (owner: orchestration-service + api).

Appendix: quick sketch of fallback_chain sample (text only)
- fallback_chain: ["us-west-adapter-v3", "eu-west-adapter-v2", "ap-southeast-proxy"]
- rollout_epoch: "2026-02-14T18:32:00Z"
- policy_signature: "sig:v1:abcd1234"

This doc is intentionally lightweight — keep comments inline in the file, mark sections that need concrete RFC work. Proposed reviewers: Diego Ramos, Priya Patel, Connor Lee, and infra-sre on-call.

End of draft.
